### Why
PR4 makes Streamable HTTP MCP honor `experimental_environment` for normal MCP traffic, but OAuth bootstrap and refresh could still use local `reqwest` before the transport was fully established.

That breaks remote-only servers whose OAuth metadata or token endpoints are reachable from the selected runtime environment but not from the orchestrator.

This PR keeps the browser-facing OAuth flow on the orchestrator while routing the non-browser OAuth HTTP work through the selected `HttpClient`.

### What
- Discover OAuth metadata through the existing `HttpClient` path instead of local orchestrator-only HTTP.
- Rewrite token and registration endpoints through a small localhost proxy so RMCP can keep using its internal `reqwest`-based OAuth flows.
- Forward proxy requests back through the selected `HttpClient`, so local servers stay local and remote servers use the remote runtime.
- Keep the proxy alive alongside `OAuthPersistor` so later token refreshes continue to follow the same path.
- Add file docs and comments in `oauth_http_client.rs` to explain why the bridge exists and what stays orchestrator-owned.

### Verification
- `just fix -p codex-rmcp-client`
- `just fmt`
- online CI

### Stack
1. #18581 protocol
2. #18582 runner
3. #18583 RMCP client
4. #18584 manager wiring and integration coverage
5. this PR: OAuth bootstrap over `HttpClient`
items.title: [5/5] Route OAuth bootstrap through HttpClient

## Why
Customer needs managed requirements to allow granular approval policies without enumerating every combination of granular flags. Before this change, `allowed_approval_policies` compared concrete `AskForApproval` objects exactly, so allowing any granular approval-policy shape meant listing every permutation.

This adds a scoped wildcard for the granular policy family only. It does not add a global `any` approval-policy escape hatch.

## What Changed
- `requirements.toml` can now include `{ granular = "any" }` in `allowed_approval_policies`.
- Config parsing stores approval allow-list entries as `ApprovalPolicyConstraint`, where concrete policies still exact-match and `{ granular = "any" }` matches any `AskForApproval::Granular(_)`.
- `configRequirements/read` now exposes the same constraint shape as `ApprovalPolicyConstraint`, preserving `{ "granular": "any" }` for clients instead of collapsing it into one concrete granular policy.
- App-server schema and generated TypeScript fixtures were regenerated for the new constraint type.

## Validation
- `cargo test -p codex-config allowed_approval_policies`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server-protocol`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server map_requirements_toml_to_api_preserves_any_granular_approval_constraint`
items.title: Allow any granular approval requirement

items.body:
## Summary

Makes `thread/archive` idempotent when the requested parent thread is already archived.

The only behavior change is that the archive handler reads the parent thread with `include_archived: true`, matching the descendant handling it already had. If the parent is already archived, it now returns a successful empty archive response instead of surfacing `no rollout found for thread id`.

## Why

Users in `#codex-app-feedback` reported that archiving a task/thread could show `Failed to archive conversation`, with the sidebar row disappearing briefly and then returning. Several reports also had the "Worktree cleaned up" banner, but the cleanup path appears to run only after a successful archive response, so that looks like a red herring rather than the direct cause.

The likely failure mode is:

1. The app still has a visible/stale active row for a thread that the server already considers archived.
2. The user archives it again.
3. The server tries to read the parent using the active-only path.
4. Because the rollout has already moved to archived storage, the request fails.

That is a poor user experience and it violates the product invariant we want: visible active threads should never be archived. Enforcing the UI invariant is still worthwhile, but this server-side change is a very small, safe backstop that prevents users from getting stuck when stale UI state leaks through.

## Safety

- Does not change the API shape.
- Does not change worktree cleanup behavior.
- Keeps `thread_archive_requires_materialized_rollout` intact: archiving a thread that never materialized a rollout still fails.
- Only turns "archive something already archived" into a no-op success.
- Adds regression coverage for archive -> archive again.

## Tests

- `just fmt`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server thread_archive_is_idempotent_for_already_archived_thread`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server suite::v2::thread_archive`
items.title: Make thread archive idempotent for archived threads

## Why
Codex users can already use built-in slash commands, but repeated personal workflows still have to be pasted into the composer by hand. This adds a private prompt-command directory so users can keep reusable prompts in their Codex home and invoke them through the same TUI slash-command flow.

## What changed
- Load private Markdown command files from `$CODEX_HOME/commands/**/*.md`.
- Use the Markdown filename as the slash command name, with subdirectories reserved for organization.
- Parse optional `description` and `argument-hint` frontmatter for slash-popup display.
- Expand `$ARGUMENTS` and positional placeholders such as `$1` and `$2` when dispatching a private command.
- Show private commands in the TUI slash popup and dispatch them as normal user prompts, including queued turns.
- Document the private command format in `docs/slash_commands.md`.

## Safety behavior
Private commands submit prompt text only. They do not pre-execute command substitutions or apply tool-restriction frontmatter, and generated prompts keep shell escaping disabled so a prompt beginning with `!` is sent to the model instead of being treated as a local command.

## Why

This is stacked on #19234. That PR makes app-server log capture expose a small `LogWriter` boundary: a tracing `Layer` that can also flush accepted log entries. This PR adds the remote gRPC implementation for that boundary so the feedback log sink can move from local SQLite-only capture toward the cloud-agent hook path without reintroducing a shared buffered-sink abstraction.

The remote sink intentionally owns its own bounded queue and worker because its write semantics differ from SQLite: batches are sent as best-effort unary RPC attempts with timeouts, and failed batches are dropped rather than retried or durably buffered on the Rust side.

## What Changed

- Added the `codex-feedback-log-sink` crate to the workspace.
- Added the `codex.feedback_log_sink.v1` generated protocol with unary `AppendLogBatch`.
- Added conversion helpers from `codex_state::LogEntry` to `FeedbackLogEntry` / `AppendLogBatchRequest`.
- Added `GrpcFeedbackLogSinkLayer`, which implements `tracing_subscriber::Layer` and `codex_state::log_db::LogWriter`.
- The gRPC layer formats tracing events into `LogEntry`, batches accepted entries by count/time, sends `AppendLogBatch`, and exposes a flush barrier for tests/shutdown.

## Testing

- `cargo test -p codex-feedback-log-sink`
- `just fix -p codex-feedback-log-sink`
- `just bazel-lock-update`
- `just bazel-lock-check`

The new fake-server test proves a representative tracing event is formatted and delivered through `AppendLogBatch` on flush.

## Why

Fixes #19596.

The `codex-tui` fallback tests for `attach_live_thread_for_selection` exercise the embedded app-server path, which can exceed the default test-thread stack in debug builds. When that happens, the process aborts with a stack overflow before the tests can report a normal assertion result. The issue was reported on Windows, and the same failure reproduced locally without increasing `RUST_MIN_STACK`.

## What changed

The two affected fallback tests now run through a small test helper that creates an explicit 4 MiB thread stack and drives the async test body with a current-thread Tokio runtime. The test behavior is unchanged: both cases still assert that empty or unmaterialized fallback threads are rejected without creating a local thread event channel.

## Verification

- `cargo test -p codex-tui attach_live_thread_for_selection_rejects_ -- --test-threads=1`

## Summary

This PR preserves `ResponseItem::Message.phase` when a message is converted through `ResponseInputItem::Message`, and records `InterAgentCommunication::to_response_input_item()` as `MessagePhase::Commentary` at the inter-agent message source.

The previous version of this PR set `MessagePhase::Commentary` in `impl From<ResponseInputItem> for ResponseItem` by parsing inter-agent message JSON. That was the wrong boundary: `ResponseInputItem::Message` can carry assistant-authored history from multiple sources, so `phase` should be data on `ResponseInputItem::Message` and should be preserved structurally.

## Context

The OpenAI API deployment checklist says follow-up requests should preserve assistant `phase`: https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/deployment-checklist#set-up-the-assistant-phase-parameter

We found this while debugging Frodex forked-agent prompt caching. Frodex was replaying the same inter-agent mailbox item as different assistant phases across root and watchdog/forked-agent requests, which changed backend tokenization and reduced shared prompt-cache prefix.

## Validation

- `cd codex-rs && just fmt`
- `cd codex-rs && cargo test -p codex-protocol response_input_message_conversion_preserves_phase -- --nocapture`
- `cd codex-rs && cargo test -p codex-protocol`
- `cd codex-rs && cargo check -p codex-core`
- `cd codex-rs && just fix -p codex-protocol`
- `cd codex-rs && just fix -p codex-core`
- `cd codex-rs && just argument-comment-lint`

items.body:
Remote compaction was rebuilding its compact prompt with the raw model-visible tool list, while normal model turns first remove any dynamic tool specs marked for deferred loading. After tool discovery started enabling deferred dynamic tools more often, compact requests could carry `defer_loading` entries into a compact path that may not preserve the paired top-level `tool_search` tool, producing the `tools.defer_loading requires tools.tool_search` failure at compaction time.

This moves the normal-turn prompt filtering into a shared helper and uses it when remote compaction builds its prompt. The compact request now sees the same model-visible tool set as an ordinary turn: `tool_search` remains available for discovery, and deferred dynamic tool definitions are kept out of the prompt until searched for.

I smoke-tested the API contract against the real compact endpoint using the exact Codex App dynamic tool introduced in openai/openai#849632: `codex_app::automation_update` with `deferLoading: true`, alongside the app's other dynamic tools. A compact request that included the deferred `automation_update` tool but no top-level `tool_search` failed with the reported 400: `Invalid Value: 'tools.defer_loading'. Deferred tools require tools.tool_search.` The same request shape after filtering out deferred dynamic tool definitions returned 200 with a compacted `message` and `compaction_summary`.

As a control, the live endpoint currently accepts the raw tool list when `tool_search` is present. The bug is the fragile coupling: if `defer_loading` survives into any compact request shape where `tool_search` is absent, compaction hard-fails before model work starts. Matching normal-turn filtering removes that failure mode entirely.

Fixes #19486.
items.title: Fix remote compaction with deferred dynamic tools

Stacked on #19705.

## Why

#19705 teaches Codex how to discover hook definitions bundled inside installed plugins. This follow-up adds the local toggle semantics needed before those hooks can be surfaced in clients: users need a stable per-hook identity, the runtime needs to honor explicit enablement overrides, and app-server clients need read/write APIs for the same state.

This intentionally keeps security and trust out of scope. Hooks currently default to enabled, with a `TODO(abhinav)` marking plugin hooks as temporarily enabled-by-default until the trust model lands.

## What

- Adds `[[hooks.config]]` entries for hook enablement state in `config.toml`, with selectors for plugin, user, and project hook sources.
- Reads hook enablement overrides from the user/session config layers, mirroring the skills enablement model.
- Applies those overrides during hook discovery using stable hook keys of the form `source_relative_path:event:matcher_group_index:handler_index`.
- Adds `hooks/list` to app-server so clients can inspect plugin, local, user, session, and project hook inventory with effective `enabled` state.
- Adds `hooks/config/write` to persist hook enablement changes through a selector-shaped app-server API.
- Refactors the TOML edit path so skills and hooks share the same array-of-tables update behavior.
- Updates app-server API docs and generated config/protocol schemas.

## Test Plan

## Why

Refs #19745.

Responses stream failures are currently hard to diagnose because the client often reports only the terminal transport error. That makes it difficult to tell whether a stream was silent from the start, closed after `response.created`, stalled before durable output, stalled after text began, or completed with inconsistent response IDs.

This adds diagnostics for those lifecycle boundaries without changing retry budgets, idle timeouts, fallback policy, model behavior, or app-server protocol shape.

## What changed

- Added a private `ResponseStreamLifecycleRecorder` in `codex-api` that tracks stream attempt, transport, terminal state, response IDs, first and last event timing, output milestones, observed event kinds, and event count.
- Wired lifecycle capture into both Responses HTTP SSE and Responses WebSocket streams, including warning logs plus appended `ApiError::Stream` details for failed streams and completed streams with mismatched response IDs.
- Updated internal `ResponseEvent::Created` parsing to carry the created response ID so lifecycle capture uses parsed event data instead of reparsing raw JSON.
- Threaded stream attempt numbers from the core retry loop into `ModelClientSession`, with the existing WebSocket-to-HTTP fallback reset preserving fresh attempt numbering for the fallback transport.

## Verification

- `cargo check -p codex-api -p codex-core`
- `cargo test -p codex-api`
- `cargo test -p codex-core responses_websocket_v2_surfaces_terminal_error_without_close_handshake`
- `cargo test -p codex-otel`
items.title: Add Responses stream lifecycle diagnostics

## Why

Streamable HTTP MCP servers can run in a remote runtime, but the OAuth side paths still used local HTTP. That meant discovery, dynamic registration, token exchange, and refresh could silently originate from the user's machine even when MCP traffic itself was routed through the selected remote environment.

This change makes OAuth use the same runtime-selected HTTP client as remote MCP traffic while preserving the user-facing OAuth flow: browser interaction and the local callback listener remain on the user's machine, and tokens continue to be stored in the existing local Codex MCP OAuth store.

## What

- Add a Codex-owned OAuth HTTP helper for Streamable HTTP MCP servers.
- Route OAuth discovery, dynamic client registration, PKCE code exchange, and refresh-token exchange through the injected `HttpClient`.
- Replace stored-token OAuth startup with a Codex token provider that refreshes and persists `StoredOAuthTokens` directly.
- Teach the Streamable HTTP adapter to inject stored OAuth bearer tokens without overriding explicit Authorization headers, configured bearer tokens, or runtime auth providers.
- Keep app-server OAuth callsites thin by moving server/runtime-aware OAuth orchestration into `codex-mcp` helpers.
- Add remote OAuth regression coverage, including an unresolvable fake OAuth host and an exec-server-backed stored-token refresh path.
- Address review feedback around `mcp list` remote auth status, refresh fallback, logout persistence, and serialized refresh attempts.

## Verification

## Summary

Add an early user facing check that explains simple literal shell redirections into protected project root metadata. The check uses FileSystemSandboxPolicy for the protected metadata names and message.

## Scope

1. Add a shared shell command helper for literal protected metadata redirection targets.
2. Use that helper in debug sandbox, legacy shell, and UnifiedExec paths.
3. Use the effective FileSystemSandboxPolicy after additional permissions are merged.
4. Keep direct command creation attempts such as mkdir .codex enforced by FileSystemSandboxPolicy and the platform sandbox adapters instead of duplicating that policy in command preflight.

## Reviewer Focus

1. This PR improves the error message for simple parseable shell redirections such as printf data into .codex config.
2. It does not weaken .git, .agents, or .codex protections. Security remains in FileSystemSandboxPolicy and the platform sandbox adapters.
3. Command preflight is intentionally not a second security policy. Direct command attempts such as mkdir .codex should still be denied by sandbox enforcement rather than by a command name deny list.

# Why

Enterprises need a managed way to restrict user-added plugin marketplaces to approved sources while keeping Codex's built-in catalogs available. This gives admins a source-based allowlist for marketplace installs without turning curated or backend catalogs into managed-config surface area.

# What

- add a `strict_known_marketplaces` managed requirement with exact matching over `source_type`, normalized `source`, `ref`, and `sparse_paths`
- enforce the allowlist for configured user marketplaces when adding, discovering, installing from, and upgrading them
- keep `openai-curated` plus backend-provided catalogs intentionally outside this requirement, and document that boundary inline
- expose the requirement through `configRequirements/read` and regenerate the app-server schema/TypeScript fixtures

# Verification

- `cargo test -p codex-config deserialize_strict_known_marketplaces`
- `cargo test -p codex-core-plugins add_marketplace_sync_rejects_git_source_blocked_by_requirements_before_clone`
- `cargo test -p codex-core install_plugin_rejects_disallowed_configured_marketplace`
- `cargo test -p codex-app-server-protocol config_requirements`
- `cargo test -p codex-core-plugins -p codex-hooks`
